rounds.text: Themis Medicare Ltd benefits from a supportive macro backdrop, as the healthcare sector operates in a clear tailwind with a tailwind score of +1.04 [E76, E78]. Recent operational momentum shows strong green shoots, highlighted by a net profit surge of 279% year-on-year, alongside sequential improvements in both quarterly profits and sales [E67, E69, E70]. Market pricing reflects strong technical participation, with the stock trading comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages while boasting a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50, E51]. On a relative valuation basis, the company trades at a discount to its sector across multiple metrics, including a P/E of 28.11x versus a sector benchmark of 33.34x and an EV/EBITDA of 16.03x against a sector benchmark of 17.7x [E5, E10]. Furthermore, the business maintains a conservative balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x and actively rewards shareholders through a healthy dividend payout of 143% [E37, E59]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and longer-term horizons remains deeply negative, and the stock is burdened by pledged promoter shares [E20, E64].

The valuation of Themis Medicare Ltd is fundamentally disconnected from its underlying operational reality, evidenced by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 48 per share compared to a market price of ₹ 118, leaving a deeply negative margin of safety of -145.9% [E45, E46]. Fundamental deterioration is widespread across horizons, with 10-year profit growth at -20%, worsening to -69% over 3 years and a catastrophic -321% over the trailing twelve months alongside a -13% drop in trailing sales [E17, E19, E20, E16]. Profitability metrics further undermine the current pricing, featuring an anemic ROCE of 2.7% and ROE of 0.4%, which lag significantly behind sector benchmarks of 11.82% and 10.37% respectively [E8, E9, E11, E12]. Operating margins have collapsed into negative territory at -13% in the TTM—a steep 26 percentage point decline from three years prior—and plummeted further to -60% in the June 2026 quarter [E29, E30]. Cash generation is severely compromised, driven by negative operating cash flow of Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr for March 2026, while financial risk is heightened by high debtors of 190 days and a substantial 43.4% promoter pledge [E34, E35, E64, E65]. Institutional conviction is entirely absent, characterized by negative money flow and foreign and domestic institutional holdings resting near zero at 0.01% [E42, E43, E44]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x alongside positive short-term momentum indicators such as 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E37, E50].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 48 per share, and we acknowledge the negative trailing operating cash flows and high promoter pledging [E34, E45, E64]. However, the bear overlooks powerful, immediate operational turnarounds that validate current market sentiment, notably a dramatic net profit increase of 279% year-on-year and sequential quarterly growth in both sales and profits [E67, E69, E70]. Conceded: past multi-year profit trajectories look weak, but the company's return on assets outperforms the sector benchmark at 6.68% versus 6.35%, and its EV/EBITDA of 16.03x trades at a discount to the sector's 17.7x [E7, E10, E18]. Furthermore, the technical setup confirms strength rather than distress, with the stock trading comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50, E51]. Conceded: institutional holdings are negligible, yet insiders maintain a massive 67.10% stake, and the broader healthcare sector enjoys a robust macro tailwind score of +1.04 [E41, E42, E43, E76]. Finally, the business maintains a healthy dividend payout of 143% and a conservatively managed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.25x, proving its financial stability while executing a clear operational rebound [E37, E59, E77].

Conceded: net profit increased 279% year-on-year, and the company trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50, E51, E67]. However, pointing to a single period's profit spike ignores the multi-year wreckage of a 20% annual profit contraction over ten years, a 46% decline over five years, and a 69% drop over three years [E17, E18, E19]. Conceded: return on assets outperforms the sector at 6.68% versus 6.35%, and EV/EBITDA trades at a discount [E7, E10]. Yet that slight operational efficiency fails to translate to equity holders, given an abysmal return on equity of 0.4% and a rock-bottom ROCE of 2.7% that severely lags the 11.82% sector benchmark [E8, E9, E12]. Conceded: insiders maintain a 67.10% stake and the healthcare sector enjoys a tailwind score of +1.04 [E41, E76]. Nevertheless, insiders have pledged 43.4% of their holding, and institutional money flow registers as negative while sales continue to contract at -13% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E44, E64]. Finally, citing a dividend payout ratio of 143% while operating cash flow and free cash flow are deeply negative at minus 3 crores and minus 8 crores respectively highlights a capital-destructive distribution model rather than financial stability [E34, E35, E59].
